analyst_view.overall: Early view: Promoted Elversberg sit seventh under Vincent Wagner, have scored four against both Gladbach and Mainz and are dangerous from set pieces, but captain Lukas Pinckert went off with a knock at Dortmund. Freiburg are third with their best-scoring start in club history and dominated Union last time, though Julian Schuster rotates heavily around Conference League games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's league games have produced 35 goals in nine, and they score from free kicks and corners (two of their four against Mainz). Freiburg concede little (10 in nine), but their attack has been the most productive in the club's history at this stage.

corners.text: The site expects 9.9 corners, 5.7 for Freiburg. I lean higher: Freiburg had around two thirds of the ball against Union and win corners through Niklas Beste's and Vincenzo Grifo's crossing, and Elversberg push for corners because they score from them.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Freiburg typically pick up two or three (three at Augsburg, two against Union) and Elversberg had one player booked at Dortmund plus their coach. Nothing here points away from the number.

shots.text: The site has 28 shots, 15.9 for Freiburg. That is plausible for a Freiburg side that dominates possession, and Elversberg's 12 at home fits their attacking approach, so I see no strong reason to move it either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's finishing has been sharp in their four-goal games and Freiburg have forwards in form in Igor Matanović and Yuito Suzuki.
